findings.finding: The scountinhibit CSR (address 0x120) is defined in CSRs.scala but has NO CSRModule implementation in the supervisorLevelCSRMods list. Any access to scountinhibit by S-mode software will result in an illegal-instruction trap, violating the Sscounterenw/Smcdeleg spec which requires this CSR to exist as a masked alias of mcountinhibit.

The menvcfg.CDE (Counter Delegation Enable) bit at position 60 is completely missing from the EnvCfg bundle. The Smcdeleg extension requires menvcfg[60]=CDE as the master enable for scounteren-write delegation. Without this bit, S-mode software cannot determine whether counter delegation is active, and the hardware has no mechanism to gate the feature.

Explicit TODO comment acknowledges that the Sscounterenw extension is unsupported. This extension defines scounteren as writable (not read-only zero), and scountinhibit as a masked alias of mcountinhibit gated by mcounteren delegation bits. Neither behavior is implemented.

The M-level permit module correctly traps HPM counter accesses (cycle to hpmcounter31) from non-M-mode when the corresponding mcounteren bit is 0. This access-control path correctly implements the counter-read permission check described in the privileged spec.
The S-level permit module correctly traps HPM counter accesses from HU-mode when scounteren counter bit is 0. This implements the standard scounteren read-prohibition correctly.

The virtual-level permit module correctly implements the H-extension counter delegation chain: VU-mode access traps EX_VI if hcounteren[x]=0 OR scounteren[x]=0; VS-mode access traps EX_VI if hcounteren[x]=0. This matches the chained delegation semantics required by the privileged spec.

The noCSRIllegal detection concatenates all CSR addresses from keys of csrRwMap and emits an illegal-instruction trap when the requested address matches none. Since scountinhibit (0x120) has no entry in any CSR map, accesses correctly trap as illegal. However, this is a band-aid—the correct fix is to implement scountinhibit as a masked alias rather than trapping.
findings.snippet:
private val noCSRIllegal = (ren || wen) && Cat(csrRwMap.keys.toSeq.sorted.map(csrAddr => !(addr === csrAddr.U))).andR
private val noCSRIllegalReg = RegEnable(noCSRIllegal, ren || wen)

findings.finding: The scountinhibit address (0x120) is defined in the CSR address table and added to the write-mask table at line 516, but has no corresponding RTL module. This address-table-only definition is misleading—it suggests the CSR exists but at runtime any access silently traps as illegal instruction.

The mcounteren/hcounteren inputs to scountovf correctly chain the delegation bits: in HS mode, only HPM counters delegated through mcounteren are visible; in VS mode, both mcounteren and hcounteren must grant delegation. This correctly prevents side-channel leakage through overflow bits.
findings.snippet:
trait HasMhpmeventOfBundle { self: CSRModule[_] =>
  val ofVec = IO(Input(UInt(perfCntNum.W)))
  val privState = IO(Input(new PrivState))
  val mcounteren = IO(Input(new Counteren))
  val hcounteren = IO(Input(new Counteren))
}

findings.finding: The mcountinhibit CSR is correctly implemented as a writable M-mode CSR controlling inhibit bits for mcycle, minstret, and mhpmcounter3-31. This provides the backend state that scountinhibit would need to alias.
findings.snippet:
val mcountinhibit = Module(new CSRModule("Mcountinhibit", new McountinhibitBundle))
  .setAddr(CSRs.mcountinhibit)
